questions.stem: A book is sitting on a table. What forces act on it, and why doesn't it move?

options.text: Friction prevents it from falling through the table
Weight acts downward and the normal reaction force acts upward -- they are balanced
No forces act on it because it is stationary
Only gravity acts on it, but the table blocks it

questions.explanation: The book has two forces acting on it: its weight pulling it downward and the normal reaction force from the table pushing it upward. These forces are balanced (equal and opposite), so the resultant force is zero and the book stays at rest.
